title: An algebraically closed finitely generated field extension is finite
statement: Let $F$ and $L$ be fields [def-weil-field], and let $i:F\to L$ be a unital ring homomorphism giving a field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. Suppose $L$ is algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and there are finitely many $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in L$ such that $L=i(F)(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$, the smallest subfield containing $i(F)$ and these elements. Then $L/F$ through $i$ is a finite extension [def-pc-field-tower], that is, $L$ is finite-dimensional as an $F$-vector space. No algebraic-closedness assumption is imposed on $F$.

source.place: Tag 030F, lemma-transcendence-degree, and Tag 09GH, lemma-algebraic-finitely-generated, provide the transcendence-basis and finite-algebraic-generation background. The additional Eisenstein obstruction for an algebraically closed target is an agent-written argument retained in report.md, extracted from the old residue-field argument of lem-trf-node-algebraically-closed-extension.

proof.text: The unital map $i$ is injective: its kernel is an ideal of the field $F$, and cannot contain $1$. Identify $F$ with its image in $L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-generated-field-finite-transcendence-basis], choose a finite transcendence basis $t_1,\ldots,t_r$ and set $K=F(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$. Thus every $a_j$ is algebraic over $K$, and $L=K(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$: each side contains the generators of the other. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-generators-finite-extension], $L/K$ is finite. Put $d=\dim_K L$.

source.place: Tags 030F (lemma-transcendence-degree), 09GH (lemma-algebraic-finitely-generated); agent-written algebraically-closed-target obstruction using the cited binomial and degree-bound statements.

proof.text: Suppose $r\geq1$ and put $m=d+1\geq1$. By [lem-trf-rational-parameter-binomial-irreducible], $p=X^m-t_1$ is irreducible in $K[X]$. It is monic of degree $m$: its leading coefficient is $1$, its constant coefficient is $-t_1$, and all intervening coefficients vanish. Viewed in $L[X]$ it is still a nonconstant polynomial, so algebraic closedness [def-weil-algebraic-closure] gives $\alpha\in L$ with $p(\alpha)=0$. Apply [lem-trf-irreducible-root-degree-bound] to the finite extension $L/K$ from Step 1. It gives $d+1=m=\deg p\leq d$, a contradiction. Hence $r=0$.

source.place: Tags 030F (lemma-transcendence-degree), 09GH (lemma-algebraic-finitely-generated); agent-written algebraically-closed-target obstruction using the cited binomial and degree-bound statements.

proof.text: For $r=0$, the field generated by the empty family over $F$ is $F$ itself. Thus $K=F$, and the finite-dimensionality of $L/K$ already proved in Step 1 is exactly the required finite-dimensionality over $F$. Transporting scalars back through the injection $i$ gives the assertion for the originally specified extension.

The item statement is unchanged from base and true: an algebraically closed field that is finitely generated as a field over F is finite over F. Step 1: the cited Stacks 030F and 09GH leaves give a finite transcendence basis t, and L=K(a) is finite over K=F(t) with d=[L:K]. Step 2: for r>=1, X^{d+1}-t_1 is irreducible over K by the new Eisenstein node, has a root in L because L is algebraically closed, and the degree-bound leaf then gives d+1<=d, a contradiction. Step 3 (r=0) is elementary. I checked n=0, r=1, and characteristic p with p dividing m. The new binomial node is true: Eisenstein at (T) over H=F(t_2..t_r) plus the monic Gauss lemma; checked on X^2-t over F_2(t). It does not restate the item, and it is not a duplicate of lem-weil-pbc-x-pow-p-minus-t-irreducible (prime p only) or lem-per-eisenstein-prime-ideal-criterion (general criterion). The Mathlib leaf matches minpoly.eq_of_irreducible_of_monic (Field.lean:136) and minpoly.natDegree_le (Finite.lean:37), both read. My DAG duplicate search found nothing.
